name: agy-bridge

hlido_opinion.headline: A small, unusually well-engineered MCP bridge that lets Claude Code offload token-heavy grunt work to Google's Antigravity CLI — high craft, honest about its own failure modes, but a niche tool for a specific two-CLI setup.
hlido_opinion.body: agy-bridge does one narrow thing and does it with more engineering discipline than most products ten times its size. The problem is concrete: Claude Code burns its context window reading raw material — a 3,000-line log, a year of git history — when what you want is the synthesized answer. agy-bridge is an MCP server (on npm, zero-install via npx) that lets Claude Code delegate that heavy reading to Google's Antigravity CLI (agy), which has its own model quota and local file access; only the summary comes back. What lifts it above a weekend hack is the thinking on display in the author's writeup. Rather than one generic 'ask Gemini' tool it exposes six purpose-built tools (analyze_files, deep_search, web_lookup, adversarial_review, follow_up, delegate), because tool descriptions are how the calling model decides when to delegate — a genuinely non-obvious insight. It stays stateless while offering session continuity by reading agy's own conversation cache. Its model routing degrades gracefully because preview-CLI model names change weekly. Most tellingly, v0.2.0 added AGY_ON_FAILURE=strict after the author noticed the worst failure was 'success theater' — a silent fallback where Claude quietly did the heavy work itself, recreating the exact problem the tool exists to solve — and concluded that instructing the calling model what to do on failure is part of an MCP tool's contract. Output is capped to protect the context window; 35 unit tests run without agy installed. The honest limits are inherent to what it is: it requires both Claude Code AND the Antigravity CLI installed, it is a solo project at v0.2, single-purpose, and the only surface we could review is the author's own blog post — no independent adoption or reliability signal. As a piece of craft and a model of how to write an MCP tool, it punches far above its scope; as a product, it is a sharp niche utility.

tier_rationale: FADING (66) — a deliberately narrow score for a deliberately narrow tool. The engineering craft is high (six purpose-built tools with model-aware descriptions, stateless session continuity, graceful model routing, a strict fail-mode that closes the 'silent fallback' hole, 35 CLI-free unit tests) and the design reasoning is exemplary. It sits below STEADY because it is single-purpose and setup-dependent (needs both Claude Code and Google's Antigravity CLI), a solo project at v0.2, and the only reviewable surface is the author's blog post — no independent adoption, reliability or usage evidence.
what_it_does_well: Offloads token-heavy reading (large logs, git archaeology) from Claude Code to agy, returning only the synthesized answer
Exposes six purpose-built tools whose descriptions give the calling model concrete triggers to delegate — not one generic tool
Stays stateless while offering session continuity by reading agy's own conversation cache and returning a follow-up ID
Routes each tool through a graceful model-preference chain, so churning preview-CLI model names don't break it
Fails loudly by design: AGY_ON_FAILURE=strict stops Claude from silently doing the heavy work itself
Caps output to protect the very context window it exists to save; 35 unit tests run with no agy install or network
what_it_fails_at: Requires both Claude Code and Google's Antigravity CLI (agy) installed — a narrow two-tool prerequisite
Single-purpose delegation bridge; not a general-purpose agent capability
Solo project at v0.2 with no independent adoption, reliability or usage evidence on the surface
The only reviewable surface is the author's own blog post — no product site, docs portal or third-party validation
Value depends on agy's Gemini quota and behaviour, an external preview CLI outside the bridge's control
best_for: Developers already running Claude Code alongside Google's Antigravity CLI who want to conserve Claude's context window
Workflows with recurring token-heavy tasks — large-file analysis, repo-wide git archaeology, adversarial code review
Engineers who value a delegation tool that fails loudly rather than silently reverting to expensive local work
Anyone studying how to design MCP tools well — the writeup is a strong reference
not_recommended_for: Users who don't run Google's Antigravity CLI (the bridge has nothing to delegate to)
Teams needing a supported, multi-contributor product with reliability guarantees
General agent tasks beyond offloading heavy reading/analysis
Buyers who require documentation and adoption evidence beyond an author blog post

evidence_urls.claim: MCP server on npm (npx -y agy-bridge) delegating heavy work from Claude Code to agy/Gemini
Six purpose-built tools with per-tool model routing chains
AGY_ON_FAILURE=strict prevents silent local fallback; output capped; 35 unit tests
Independent adoption or reliability evidence beyond the author's blog

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: First-class MCP for Claude Code: add agy-bridge to mcpServers (command npx, args -y agy-bridge) and Claude Code gains six delegation tools. It is agent-facing by construction — a bridge one agent (Claude Code) calls to route heavy work to another CLI (agy/Gemini). Requires the Antigravity CLI installed locally to function.

marking_signal.reason: agy-bridge is a delegation bridge between coding-agent CLIs and does not itself generate published synthetic content, so Article-50 output-marking obligations do not attach.

summary: A small, unusually well-engineered MCP bridge that lets Claude Code offload token-heavy grunt work to Google's Antigravity CLI — high craft, honest about its own failure modes, but a niche tool for a specific two-CLI setup.
